issues.reason: Sealing the antecedent as `(And (Member sk_air_1 air))` records "there IS air" as the counterfactual's antecedent, which is the positive form the registered seal-polarity limitation explicitly bars ("seal what is expressible and leave the negated conjunct out … not a licence to assert the positive form").

The sealed consequent records a bare `(Can sk_live_1)` with a duration measure, i.e. "people could live for ten minutes" — the opposite of the stated "could not live" — the same positive-in-place-of-negated substitution.

With a NEGATIVE antecedent the recipe's "antecedent proposition at strength 0.0" is the double negation of "there is no air", i.e. exactly "there is air" — the presupposition the subjunctive carries — so the top-level atom is true of the sentence's content and the mechanical strength-0.0 wording simply cannot apply here (the reviewer's own third gap says so).

A focus atom's filler slot takes the focused constituent's symbol or, for predicate focus, the verb-class lemma; the bare native integer `10` is neither, and it spuriously cross-references the magnitude inside the `Measure` atom, so the atom is ill-typed.

It stands that the instruction set's own worked example gives `live` an `Agent` subject, so a QA mismatch is a real risk; it is overstated as a contradiction, because the intransitive-subject test independently licenses `Experiencer` for a stative intransitive and this sense (be alive / survive) is not the example's sense (reside) — the atom is neither false nor ill-typed.

It stands that a bare plural is generic by the determiner test and a group witness is the definite-plural device; it is overstated because the licensed generic form is an `Implication` rule, which cannot be nested inside a `Counterfactual` seal (its free variables would have to cross the seal boundary), so no licensed alternative existed and the group witness is well-typed and asserts nothing at top level.

gaps_confirmed: negated-antecedent conditional ("if there were no air") — the instruction set states outright that "unless X" / "if not X" is not yet supported
"were"-subjunctive present counterfactual — `Counterfactual` is specified only for the past "if X had V-ed, Y would have V-ed" form
the counterfactual presupposition recipe collides with a negative antecedent: the prescribed strength-0.0 antecedent bundle is a double negation there
negation inside a seal generally — a sealed clause has no polarity carrier, so "could not live" is unrepresentable
scalar minimizer "not even ten minutes" — a focus particle over a measured duration has no symbol to use as its filler
new_gaps: a generic bare-plural subject inside a seal has no licensed form at all: the generic's `Implication` rule cannot be written as a term, since rule variables cannot cross a seal boundary

`live` is left underdetermined between `Agent` (the worked example, reside sense) and `Experiencer` (the stative-intransitive test, be-alive sense), so the same lemma can take two roles and QA stops matching
repair_summary: Removed the entire `(Counterfactual …)` atom: both sealed clauses recorded the positive of an unexpressible negation ("there is air", "people could live ten minutes"), and since the negation scopes over everything contentful in each clause, nothing expressible remains to seal — deleting `(Can …)` or `(Member sk_air_1 air)` alone would still leave a false sealed record, which the calibration line forbids. The ill-typed `(Even 10 sk_live_1)` went with it. Kept the top-level `(Member sk_air_1 air)` untouched — it is the counterfactual's own presupposition and no confirmed issue names it.
notes: The repair is very lossy, but every removed atom recorded the opposite of what the sentence says; the residue asserts only the presupposed existence of air. This item is a clean instance of the negated-antecedent / negation-in-a-seal pair of gaps, not of parser carelessness.
